discovery: Pulsar timing arrays and the evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany

motivation: These three scientists turned an array of millisecond pulsars across the Galaxy into a gravitational-wave detector. Manchester founded the Parkes Pulsar Timing Array and helped build the International Pulsar Timing Array. Kramer led the European effort and pushed pulsar timing to precision tests of general relativity. McLaughlin co-founded NANOGrav and led it for many years. Their collaborations spent almost two decades timing pulsars to nanosecond precision. In 2023 NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA, PPTA and CPTA each published evidence for a stochastic gravitational-wave background at nanohertz frequencies, and the data show the Hellings-Downs angular correlation predicted by general relativity. This opens a new band of the gravitational-wave spectrum, most likely from supermassive black-hole binaries. It complements LIGO and gives a new way to probe galaxy evolution and the early universe.
